final_text:
## Incident Report — Malware Infection, DESKTOP-H8ALZBV

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 packets, 2024-08-15 04:09:43–04:42:26 UTC+4, ~32 min). No Suricata/IDS export was present in the evidence directory; findings are derived entirely from packet-level analysis with `tshark`.

### Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** (confirmed via DHCP option 12 and NBNS name registrations) |
| AD domain | lafontainebleu.org (NetBIOS: LAFONTAINEBLEU), DC = WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS at 10.8.15.4 |
| Logged-in Windows user | **plucero** (repeated Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges with CNameString `plucero` between 10.8.15.133 and the DC 10.8.15.4) |

### Malware family

**SecTopRAT (Arechclient2)** — attribution is **behavioral/TTP-based, not signature-confirmed**. No AV/YARA/IDS artifact was present in this evidence set to provide a hash or rule match. The call is based on a distinctive, reproducible protocol fingerprint observed directly in the capture:
- Persistent plaintext HTTP beacon on port 80 to a single hardcoded IP (no DNS lookup ever performed for it — the IP is embedded in the malware, not resolved).
- Fixed, malformed User-Agent with the tell-tale extra space: `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`.
- Binary/encrypted payload smuggled inside an oversized base64 `Cookie:` header (static per-session bot ID) rather than in the HTTP body, on both GET and POST requests to `/`.
- Delivery mechanism (invoice-themed ZIP → padded multi-MB JS dropper → BITSAdmin-fetched DLL from the same C2 IP) matches the known SecTopRAT distribution chain.

### Infection timeline (all times UTC+4, as recorded in the pcap)

1. **04:10:58** — 10.8.15.133 requests `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?...` (resolves to Cloudflare-fronted IPs 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159). Server returns `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Invoice 876597035_003.zip"`.
2. ZIP contains a single JScript file, **`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`** (6.99 MB, padded with ~7 MB of unrelated junk text from unrelated public documents — a known AV file-size-threshold evasion trick). Embedded inside the padding is the redirect URL `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent`, matching the DNS query for `business.checkfedexexp.com` seen at frame 9026-9027.
3. **04:11:59** — 10.8.15.133 uses Microsoft BITS (`User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8`) to `HEAD`/`GET` `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — a **159,232-byte PE32+ x86-64 DLL**.
4. **04:11:59 onward, continuously through end of capture (04:42:26)** — 10.8.15.133 opens 300+ short-lived TCP sessions to `72.5.43.29:80` (approx. one request every ~6 seconds), sending GET/POST `/` requests carrying an encrypted payload in the `Cookie` header — active C2 check-in traffic.

### Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — hardcoded C2 IP, contacted directly (no DNS lookup), 300+ GET/POST beacon requests over ~30 minutes

**Malicious/phishing infrastructure**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 — Cloudflare-fronted)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (172.67.170.159, 104.21.55.70)

**Malicious URL**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` (initial ZIP delivery)
- `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent` (redirect URL embedded in the JS dropper)
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (second-stage DLL fetch via BITSAdmin)

**Transferred files and hashes (SHA-256, computed locally from objects extracted out of the pcap)**

| File | Size | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| Invoice 876597035_003.zip | 2,767,804 bytes | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` |
| Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js | 6,990,020 bytes | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` |
| 0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4 (2nd-stage DLL, PE32+ x86-64) | 159,232 bytes | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

### Recommendation
Isolate DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133) from the network immediately, reset the `plucero` account credentials (and any credentials cached/typed on that host), and block `72.5.43.29`, `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, and `business.checkfedexexp.com` at the perimeter. Given the RAT capability implied by SecTopRAT and 30 minutes of active C2 dwell time, treat the host as fully compromised — reimage rather than clean.
